introduction: Christmas joy fills our hearts: the Word became flesh and lived among us. God, who once spoke through the prophets, now speaks to us through his Son, born in Bethlehem. Today we celebrate not only a birth long ago but the light that shines in every darkness. As we gather with the whole Church, let us adore the Child of Bethlehem and welcome him with grateful hearts.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: On this holy day, God has given us his Son. With joy and confidence, let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church throughout the world: that she may proclaim with joy that God is with us, and bring the light of Christ to every nation. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peace on earth: that the Prince of Peace may end war and violence, especially in the Holy Land where he was born. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the poor, the homeless, refugees and all who have no room this Christmas: that they may find shelter and kindness. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the sick, the lonely and the grieving: that the light of Christmas may bring them comfort and hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our families and our parish: that the love of the Christ Child may unite us and make us generous to all. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Loving Father, in the birth of your Son you have shown us your glory. Hear the prayers of your people on this joyful day, and let the light of Christ shine in our lives. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The Word became flesh
reflection.body:
At the Mass during the day on Christmas, the Church does not read the story of the manger. That story belongs to the night. In the light of day, she reads the opening of John's Gospel, which tells us who this child is.

"In the beginning was the Word." Before anything was made, the Word was with God and was God. Through him all things came into being. In him was life, and that life was the light of all people. Then comes the sentence on which all of Christmas rests: "The Word became flesh and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the only born Son of the Father, full of grace and truth."

The Letter to the Hebrews says the same thing in another way. God spoke "in the past" through the prophets, "at many times and in various ways," but now he "has at the end of these days spoken to us by his Son." Jesus is not one more message from God. He is God's Word in person.

That is the wonder of Christmas. The God who made the stars became a child who needed to be fed and held. He did not save us from a distance. He entered our history, our families, our poverty and our pain.

Isaiah pictures a messenger running across the mountains with good news, and watchmen shouting for joy because they see the Lord returning to Zion. Christmas is that good news. God has come home to his people.

John is also honest about darkness. "The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn't overcome it." He does not say there is no darkness, but that it cannot win. Many people will celebrate Christmas this year in grief, illness, poverty or fear. The Christmas message is especially for them.

Today let us kneel in spirit at the manger, adore the Word made flesh, and carry his light to someone who needs it.
